title: FeasibilityEnvelope
description: Operator + Professor's joint declaration of what the harness ACTUALLY has access to at production-entry time, before any claim is designed. This anchors strong+safe claim construction: a 'deployment-grade' claim cannot be promised if the matching resource (real data, live LLM, compute budget) is not in the envelope. Validators reject mismatches at design_initial_claim_contract and revise_root_after_reject time.

data_sources_available.description: What data the harness can actually read for this thread. Each entry is either an adapter_id registered under settings.json.data_adapters (real data path) or the literal string 'synthetic' (the harness can generate). 'synthetic' alone forbids deployment-scope claims.

scope_note.description: Brief description of what this data covers — date range, universe, asset class, etc.

llm_oracles_available.description: What LLM oracles are reachable: 'subscription_claude_code' (Claude Code interactive driving the thread itself, free), 'live_anthropic_api' (paid, requires billing_ack), 'deterministic_proxy' (no LLM, deterministic substitute), or 'none'. Live API entries require operator ack flags in settings.

compute_budget.description: Practical compute envelope. The Professor uses these to scope claims that fit — e.g., a 19,200-measurement experiment may need to be chunked.

baseline_provenance_available.description: Baselines that exist with verifiable paper / arxiv / repo provenance via the market_research dossier. self-made baselines are NOT listed here.

provenance.description: arxiv id, doi, repo url, or reference_papers/ filename

operator_intent.description: What kind of outcome the operator is willing to accept as 'goal achieved'. target = preferred; acceptable_alternative_scopes = fallback options before the system gives up scope-wise (it never gives up the user-goal+AC-accept dual-gate, but it may settle for narrower deploy-grade than 'deployment' if real data is missing).

external_falsifier.description: ADR 0006: the harness-owned check that goal-achievement is graded against, registered BEFORE the claim is designed and OWNED by the operator (or supervisor auto-bootstrap acting as operator stand-in) — never by the production tree-search. 'kind=none' (or absence) caps max_attestable_status at 'unverified_screen': achieved=true becomes structurally impossible. A passing falsifier_result computed against holdout_source_id is the only path to achieved=true.

kind.description: real_holdout = predicate evaluated on a registered real_adapter (strong falsifier). cross_generator_transfer = ranking preserved on a held-out DISTINCT generator B (weak air-gapped falsifier). none = no falsifier; ceiling is unverified_screen.

holdout_source_id.description: real_adapter id (real_holdout) or the held-out generator-B label (cross_generator_transfer). MUST differ from the data source the worker fit on. Required unless kind=none.

predicate.description: The deterministic pass condition the harness computes over the holdout. For cross_generator_transfer, metric is the rank-correlation key (e.g. 'spearman_rho').

registered_by.description: Who registered this falsifier. 'worker' is intentionally absent from the enum — the success-seeking run must not author its own falsifier.

max_attestable_status.description: Harness-STAMPED at submit_feasibility_envelope time from external_falsifier (NOT operator-writable). 'goal_achieved' only when a falsifier with kind!=none is registered; otherwise 'unverified_screen'. The attestation gate refuses achieved=true when this is 'unverified_screen'.

execution_constraints.description: Operator-declared deterministic constraints the harness enforces at experiment-design time (design_experiment_template). General across domains — the operator names whatever tooling a thread must use; the harness only checks, it never authors the experiment.

required_modules.description: Python modules every experiment in this thread MUST import. A cheap deterministic gate (string scan at submission), NOT an LLM critic: e.g. ['backtester'] forces the operator's registered evaluator over a hand-rolled substitute; ['torch'] for an ML thread. design_experiment_template rejects submitted source that does not import each one.
